title: Ureter, Urinary Bladder - Anatomy Lecture
department_desc: Anatomy and embryonic development of the kidneys, ureters, bladder and urethra
matrix_title: TWISTED MEDICINE LECTURE 2 - HIGH-YIELD ANATOMICAL PEARLS & BOARD EXAM MATRIX

summary_table.content: • 1. Ureteropelvic Junction (UPJ): Level of L1 vertebra where renal pelvis narrows into ureter. • 2. Pelvic Brim Crossing: Bifurcation of Common Iliac / External Iliac vessels over sacroiliac joint.
• 3. Ureterovesical Junction (UVJ): Intramural oblique tunnel (1.5-2 cm); narrowest site (3 mm) -> primary stone impaction &
• Female (Water Under the Bridge'): Ureter passes INFERIOR and POSTERIOR to Uterine Artery (1.5-2 cm lateral to cervix).

Extreme risk of accidental clamping during hysterectomy! • Male: Crossed anteriorly and superiorly by Ductus (Vas) Deferens near the base of the bladder. • Epithelium: Transitional epithelium (Urothelium). Star-shaped lumen on cross-section. • Muscularis: Upper 2/3 = 2 layers (Inner Longitudinal, Outer Circular). Lower 1/3 = 3 layers (Inner Long, Middle Circ, Outer
• Arterial Supply: Segmental anastomoses from Renal, Gonadal, Aorta, Common/Internal Iliac, Inferior Vesical, Uterine
• Location: Pelvic organ in adults; abdominal in infants (up to 6 years). Capacity: 220-300 mL. • Apex: Gives attachment to Median Umbilical Ligament (fibrous remnant of embryonic Urachus).

• Trigone: Permanently smooth triangle (no submucosa) on internal base. Bounded by 2 ureteric orifices (Interureteric crest / Fold of Mercier) and internal urethral orifice. • Embryology: Trigone derived from Mesoderm (Mesonephric ducts); rest of bladder from Endoderm (urogenital sinus). • Parasympathetic (S2, S3, S4): Pelvic splanchnic (Nervi erigentes) -> M3 receptors contracts Detrusor & relaxes internal sphincter -> Motor to voiding.
• Sympathetic (T11-L2): Hypogastric nerves -> Beta-2 relaxes Detrusor, Alpha-1 contracts Internal Sphincter -> Urine storage

& prevents retrograde ejaculation. • Somatic (S2, S3, S4): Pudendal Nerve -> contracts External Urethral Sphincter -> Voluntary retention. • Automatic (Spastic) Bladder: Cord transection above S2 -> intact spinal reflex arc -> periodic involuntary reflex emptying. • Atonic (Tabetic) Bladder: Destruction of S2-S4 sensory afferents (Tabes dorsalis, Diabetes) - loss of urge -> massive
distension & Overflow Incontinence. • Patent Urachus (Urachal Fistula): Continuous urine discharge from umbilicus due to failure of urachus obliteration.
